title: release-security-exception-logbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact working log for handling release-time security deviations, approvals, and the automation we use to collect evidence for sign-off. It lives as the canonical lightweight companion to the full Release Security Acceptance Playbook (see linked artifacts). Use it for fast triage of exceptions and as the source of records pushed to SIEM exporters.

Overview of the process (short):
- Release engineer opens a release ticket and flags any deviations from the standard security checklist.
- Security reviewer (role: release-approver) evaluates the deviation, assigns exception risk level, and either approves, requests remediation, or escalates.
- Evidence automation collects logs and artifacts, attaches them to the ticket and sends a digest to SIEM and Compliance bucket.
- If exception approved, approval is recorded with metadata (approver, scope, expiry) in the exceptions registry.

Common deviation categories we see:
- RBAC drift: temporary role granted to expedite rollout (example: granting "release-executor" to a contractor for 48h).
- Incomplete audit evidence: missing KV cache telemetry or truncated request/response pairs.
- Service account keys not rotated per policy due to last-minute infra change.
- Temporary bypass of canary routing due to capacity constraints.

RBAC v2 quick mapping (practical):
- release-requestor: can open release tickets and attach artifacts. No deployment rights.
- release-executor: can trigger deployment pipelines for specified environments; audited scope limited by tag (prod/dedicated/private).
- release-approver (security): can approve exceptions; approval must include expiry and compensating controls.
- security-observer: read-only access to release logs, can add comments/evidence.
- infra-admin: full rights; exceptions for infra-admin require at least 2 approvers due to high risk.

Approval template (copy/paste for ticket):
- Exception ID: EXC-YYYY-NNN
- Requestor: <name/email>
- Short description: <what changed and why>
- Risk level: Low | Medium | High (justify in one sentence)
- RBAC change (if any): <role added/modified>
- Compensating controls: <e.g., 48h two-factor approval, increased logging>
- Evidence attachments: <list of artifacts or automation outputs>
- Approver(s): <name(s)>
- Approval expiry: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Post-approval checklist: <revert steps, validation queries, owner>

Minimal acceptance checklist (pre-signoff):
- All modified permissions documented (role, principal, timebound)
- Audit stream contains entries for: permission grant, deployment start, deployment end, and any errors
- Evidence automation has at least one sampled request/response for the release window
- SIEM digest contains parsed fields (see schema) and no parsing errors
- Compensating control verified (e.g., alert rule active)

Audit log schema (fields we require in release context):
- event_id (uuid)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- principal (user/service account id)
- action (grant_role | revoke_role | deploy_start | deploy_end | api_call)
- resource (string; e.g., cluster:prod/gpu-pool-3)
- role (if applicable)
- outcome (success | failure | partial)
- correlation_id (release ticket id or workflow id)
- extra (free text for context)

Note: schema above is intentionally small; full schema in docs.redwood.ai/audit-schema-v2. Automation must always include correlation_id for traceability.

SIEM export mapping (example to Splunk/Datadog/SumoLogic):
- event_id -> id
- timestamp -> @timestamp
- principal -> user.id or service.account
- action -> event.action
- resource -> resource.path
- role -> access.role
- outcome -> event.outcome
- correlation_id -> trace.correlation_id

Pipeline sketch for Evidence Automation (working):
1) Release ticket created with tag:security-exception: true. Ticket triggers webhook to automation endpoint.
2) Collector AWS Lambda (or GCF) queries internal auditstore for correlation_id and timeframe, pulls matching logs, and runs a set of validators (schema check, presence check, sample extraction).
3) Collector stores artifacts in a timeboxed S3 bucket (prefix: exceptions/EXC-YYYY-NNN/) and writes a summary JSON to the ticket and the SIEM forwarder.
4) SIEM forwarder enriches events (geo, aws_account, infra_stage) and forwards to Splunk index: security:releases.

Practical note: avoid storing full PII/SECRET blobs in S3. Use smart redaction lambda that masks tokens/keys but keeps shape for debugging.

Sample validation queries (sane defaults):
- "count by action where correlation_id=EXC-YYYY-NNN and timestamp within last 2 hours" -> expect >= 3 (grant, deploy_start, deploy_end)
- "search outcome=failure AND correlation_id=EXC-YYYY-NNN" -> expect 0 (unless flagged)

Escalation matrix (short):
- Low: security reviewer + release owner approve.
- Medium: security reviewer + eng manager or product owner.
- High: security reviewer + two approvers (one must be security lead) + CTO notified.
- Always notify compliance@redwood.ai for private deployments or regulated customers.

Record-keeping and retention:
- Approved exceptions are recorded in the exceptions registry (immutable entry) with the following fields: exception id, approvers, scope, expiry, attachments (S3 pointers), and revocation status.
- Evidence buckets are retained per policy; default 90 days for dev/staging artifacts, 365 days for production releases tied to compliance customers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we auto-revoke RBAC grants when expiry hits? (current plan: scheduled job that looks for expired exceptions and triggers revocation pipeline; need infra ticket) - JIRA-SEC-834
- Add more structured telemetry for KV cache access during deployment to help debug quality regressions.
- Decide whether to include full diffs of role bindings in the SIEM payload (privacy concern).

Example approval log entry (freeform, human readable):
"2025-02-28 15:43Z — EXC-2025-042 — release-executor granted to contractor:j.sato for 48h to deploy hotfix for model-serving shard overflow. Approved by Rina Gomez (security) and Omar Farouk (eng). Evidence: s3://evidence/exceptions/EXC-2025-042/summary.json. SIEM event id: splunk:98765."

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Full RBAC v2 design doc: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2-ddl
- Audit schema master: docs.redwood.ai/audit-schema-v2
- SIEM forwarder config: infra/ops/siem-forwarder (internal repo)
- Automation lambda skeleton: github.com/redwood-inference/release-evidence-collector

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact. If you want a longer playbook-style doc with step-by-step screenshots, I will copy content into the Playbook. For now focus on: is the acceptance checklist complete and are the automation steps reasonable?
- If you add a collaborator, please append your initials and the date to the top of the doc.

End of logbook.

[last edited by Aisha Patel on 2025-03-01]"
